jobs.title: Staff Platform / Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description_text: About the Role: webAI runs private AI on the customer's own hardware: on-prem Apple-silicon fleets (some air-gapped), Linux servers, and the customer's own cloud. As Staff Platform/Infrastructure Engineer you'll own the substrate that makes this repeatable. That means how our kernel, services and local model inference get packaged, deployed, secured, observed and upgraded across bare metal and cloud. You'll inherit a production deployment serving a global enterprise customer, lead its move to a leaner next-generation architecture, and turn it into a deployment kit our forward-deployed engineers can use to install a new customer from the docs alone. This is a hands-on staff role: you'll make the architecture calls, write the code and carry the pager. What You'll Do: - Own deployment for the webAI kernel and B2B SDK. Deliver single-machine installs, multi-node clusters, and cloud (AWS, Azure/AKS) installs from one model, keeping the gap between cloud and bare metal small. - Choose and evolve our orchestration approach (Nomad, Kubernetes, or config-managed native services such as Ansible plus launchd) with simplicity as the goal. Cut custom infrastructure code where you can. - Run Apple-silicon fleets in production: launchd services, firewalling (pf), Lima/Docker VMs, GPU/unified-memory sizing for local LLM inference, and recovery after power loss or hardware failure. - Build the inference serving layer with the AI team: an OpenAI-compatible model gateway, conversation-pinned lo

jobs.description_text: About the Role The ACLU seeks a Spring Legal Intern in the Criminal Law Reform Project of the ACLU’s National office. This is a hybrid position based out of our National Office in New York, NY. Qualifying applicants must currently be matriculated legal students and must be based in the U.S. for the entire duration of the internship. The Team: The Criminal Law Reform Project advocates for the constitutional and civil rights of those impacted by criminal legal systems. We use litigation and advocacy to confront systemic government conduct that fuels the carceral state and police abuse, and oppresses people based on race, class, and other characteristics. CLRP does this work because everyone suspected, accused, or convicted of a crime deserves dignity, fairness, and an opportunity to thrive. Ultimately, we seek to shift power to under-resourced communities and to elevate approaches to justice and safety that advance fundamental rights for all. The Project’s current priorities are combatting police violence while bolstering individual rights against police authority; protecting the fundamental right to pretrial liberty; eliminating excessive conditions of post release supervision; and creating robust public defense systems to guarantee the constitutional right to counsel. CLRP works closely with the ACLU’s National Political Advocacy Department, our Communications Department, and our affiliates to advance an affirmative vision for criminal legal system reform. You’ll work with operations, maintenance, engineers, process owners, and R&D teams to understand how work is done, review SDSs and toxicology information, determine which exposure assessments are needed, and conduct the sampling yourself. You’ll spend most of your time where the exposures are: in machine shops, cleanroom laboratories, and R&D test areas. You'll work with engineers and scientists as they develop new technology. You’ll explain results clearly to the employees whose exposures you measure and to Antora’s leaders, then use the data and what you hear from the people doing the work to improve the program. This role combines fieldwork and practical problem-solving with the day-to-day work of maintaining exposure monitoring, controls, and health programs. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer - Vehicle Test
jobs.description_text: Senior Software Engineer - Vehicle Test We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Software Engineer to join our rapidly-growing team and improve our hardware testing capabilities. In this role, you will design the end-to-end software architecture used to validate hardware at the integrated vehicle levels as well as supporting our major HITL testbed infrastructure for flight validation, ensuring our aerospace systems are mission-ready. Your testing and infrastructure will be the ultimate safeguard ensuring our hardware and software are flight-ready. Your responsibilities include refining specifications from electrical engineers to validate critical flight components, supporting all development phases from proposal to final test, implementing ground control and telemetry software, and contributing to the team’s growth through active recruitment and hiring efforts. This role puts you at the front of the line for new hardware releases, where you will work directly in the lab to identify and fix complex issues in real-time. Because your work supports testing across all vehicle subsystems, you will gain unique insight into the entire hardware lifecycle and partner with nearly every engineering team to ensure our systems perform flawlessly under the most demanding conditions. By combining high-level architecture with hands-on validation, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring that what we send into flight stays there. jobs.location_raw: MacDill AFB, FL · Petersen SFB, CO
jobs.description_text: Role This role is for a Data Scientist on a close-knit team supporting a U.S. Special Operations Command program at MacDill AFB. This team is at the center of helping the command empower and leverage its data for more effective analysis and decision making. As a subject matter expert, the Data Scientist will leverage their experience to gather and derive insights from complex data, assist the command with development initiatives, and facilitate digital transformation efforts. The work done in this role has a direct impact on mission readiness as the team's efforts go toward making a more resilient and data-driven organization. Responsibilities A data scientist will have skills sets of both data analysts and data engineers. Data scientists are responsible for designing, implementing, and maintaining a data pipeline. In addition, data scientists shall interpret and analyze complex sets of data, as well as plan, execute, and manage ML projects with cloud-native platforms and advanced ML solutions. They understand some of the most challenging processes, technologies, and can leverage a vast array of methodologies in the field, such as data mining, natural language programming, and machine learning. Data scientists must have a combination of skills that includes programming, mathematical modeling, statistics, and domain knowledge.
